subject: Biotechnology
title: Microbiome and Precision Health
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Microbiome and Precision Health.

hook.text: Your gut hosts 39 trillion bacteria — their collective genome affects drug metabolism, immunity, and mood.

buildup.text: Metagenomic sequencing profiles the microbiome — identifying which species and genes are present in your gut.

discovery.text: Gut bacteria metabolize drugs differently — cardiac drug digoxin is inactivated by certain gut bacteria in 40% of patients.

twist.text: Your microbiome changes with diet, antibiotics, and age — personalized medicine must account for a moving target.

climax.text: Fecal microbiota transplant cures recurrent C. difficile infection in over 90% of cases — microbiome as medicine.

punchline.text: Your second genome matters — the microbiome personalizes health beyond human DNA.

quiz.question: How does the microbiome complicate personalized medicine?
options: Microbiome bacteria prevent all drugs from being absorbed
Gut bacteria can metabolize drugs differently between patients, and the microbiome changes over time
The microbiome is identical in all healthy adults

details.summary: The human microbiome, comprising trillions of bacteria, influences drug metabolism, immune function, and disease susceptibility. Integrating microbiome analysis with genomic data enhances personalized medicine by predicting drug responses, disease risks, and optimal probiotic interventions for
details.whyItMatters: The microbiome modulates the effectiveness and toxicity of many drugs including cancer immunotherapy. Ignoring microbial variation means ignoring a major source of individual treatment response differences that genomics alone cannot explain.
takeaways: Gut bacteria metabolize over 150 common drugs, affecting their efficacy and toxicity
Microbiome composition predicts response to cancer immunotherapy
Combining genomic and microbiome data improves personalized treatment predictions

faq.question: How does the microbiome affect drug effectiveness?
faq.answer: Gut bacteria can activate prodrugs, inactivate active drugs, produce toxic metabolites, or compete for drug absorption. The cardiac drug digoxin is inactivated by Eggerthella lenta. Some chemotherapy drugs require bacterial metabolism for activation.

faq.question: Can microbiome testing improve cancer treatment outcomes?
faq.answer: Studies show patients with diverse gut microbiomes respond better to checkpoint immunotherapy. Specific bacteria like Akkermansia muciniphila and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii correlate with treatment success.
